topRisks: A v2026-only HTTP server rejects initialize as 404 method-not-found (with 2026 headers) or 400 header-mismatch (bare legacy initialize); stdio initialize without _meta is JSON-RPC -32022. Any in-repo launcher still sending initialize will fail.

HTTP clientId is per-POST and is not stable; no Mcp-Session-Id is minted; no McpRequestContext field is server-minted and stable across HTTP requests. Auth, rate limits, or MRTR keyed on clientId/session will not survive G4 over HTTP.
HTTP notifications/cancelled is 202-acked but does not interrupt another POST's in-flight 2026 tool call (session === undefined). Interrupt is proven on stdio only.
Default allowedOrigins is empty: any Origin header is 403. Browser-facing in-repo HTTP MCP servers must pass an allowlist.
ping, logging/setLevel, resources/subscribe, and JSON-RPC batches are gone on 2026 (404 / 400). Completions and logging capabilities are still advertised as empty objects.
decisionChallenges: G4 (v2026_07_28 only) is implementable and is the only configuration that removes initialize. Mixed lists are a supported runtime feature (at most one stateless) and keep initialize alive via the first stateful adapter, even when the client offered protocolVersion 2026-07-28.
No server-minted stable HTTP identity exists on 2026. Adopting G4 over Streamable HTTP means identity, cancellation of other POSTs, and session log levels cannot be transported the legacy way.
HTTP cancellation of in-flight 2026 work is not implemented. If beep-effect HTTP MCP servers need spec cancellation without sessions, that is a gap in Effect at a7a71921de, not a wiring bug.
In-repo HTTP launchers that omit allowedOrigins will 403 browser Origins. In-repo clients that probe ping or send initialize will fail against a v2026-only server (G6 in-scope).
grillQuestions: Confirm G4: every in-repo server protocols: [McpProtocol.v2026_07_28] only, accepting that initialize dies and mixed-list fallback is forbidden?
For HTTP MCP servers, is per-request identity (client-supplied _meta / requestState) enough, given clientId is not stable and Mcp-Session-Id is not minted?
Is it acceptable that HTTP cannot cancel a different POST's in-flight 2026 tool call, with cancellation working only on stdio?
Who owns setting allowedOrigins on each in-repo layerHttp (nlp/m365/uspto/gov-legal/practice-kg/OntologyMcpTransport), given the production default denies all Origins?
Must in-repo clients and harnesses stop sending ping and initialize, and start sending server/discover plus MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Method, Mcp-Name, and _meta clientCapabilities on every request?
Should resources/read MRTR (schema allows InputRequiredResult, handler never returns it) be treated as out of scope or as an Effect gap to track?
